# File-Based Routing

URLs come from the files and folders in `pb_pages/`.

## Pages

| File | URL |
|---|---|
| `index.ets` | `/` |
| `about.ets` | `/about` |
| `docs/index.md` | `/docs` (and `/docs/`) |
| `docs/routing.md` | `/docs/routing` |
| `products/[id].ets` | `/products/123`, with `ctx.params.id = "123"` |
| `[org]/[repo]/index.ets` | `/acme/web`, with `ctx.params = { org: "acme", repo: "web" }` |

- The extension is dropped. `index` maps to its folder.
- `[name]` matches exactly one non-empty segment. A parameter must be the whole segment: `post-[id].ets` is an error at startup.
- Segment counts must match: `products/[id].ets` doesn't match `/products/123/reviews`.
- A URL with a trailing slash matches the same route as without it. Pages never redirect to add or remove one.
- Matching is case-sensitive.

See [Accessing Parameters](/docs/extensions/pages/parameters).

## Groups

A folder named `(name)` doesn't add a URL segment. Use groups to give part of the site its own layout or middleware:

```text
pb_pages/
  (site)/
    +layout.ets     # wraps everything in (site)
    index.ets       # /
    about.ets       # /about
  xapi/
    count.ets       # /xapi/count, outside the (site) layout
```

## Code: `.ts` files

A `.ts` file runs, the way a `.php` file does. Its path is its URL, as for a page:

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `about.ts` beside `about.ets` | that page's code: `load` feeds the template, a `post` handles its form. See [Loading data](/docs/extensions/pages/loading-data#page-code). |
| `feeds/rss.ts` | an endpoint at `/feeds/rss`, with no template: its handlers send the whole response (JSON, a feed, a redirect). See [Endpoints and JSON](/docs/extensions/pages/api-routes). |
| `feeds/index.ts`, `products/[id].ts` | the folder's URL, a `[param]` route, as for pages |

Only `.ts` runs. A `.js` file is a [static file](#static-files) like any other, so browser scripts can sit anywhere in `pb_pages`. `.d.ts` files are neither served nor run.

## Static files

Every other file is served as-is at its path, with groups removed: `assets/app.css` serves `/assets/app.css`. See [Static content](/docs/extensions/pages/static-content).

## Which route wins

1. `/api/...` and `/_/...` belong to PocketBase. Pages never see them.
2. Among matching routes the most specific wins: segments are compared from the left, and a literal segment beats a `[param]`. So `products/new.ets` beats `products/[id].ets` for `/products/new`.
3. Two files can't claim the same URL: a page and a static file, or an endpoint and a page (`feed.ts` and `feed/index.ets`). A `.ts` beside a template of the same name is that page's code, not a second claim. These are startup errors.
4. A URL nothing in `pb_pages` matches goes on to `pb_public`, then to PocketBase.

## When routes change

The route table is built when the app starts and rebuilt whenever anything in `pb_pages` changes. A rebuild never restarts the app or reloads `pb_hooks`. Startup errors (bad names, conflicts) are logged with the file path, and the previous route table keeps serving.
